findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the new ADR 0106 Follow-up paragraph, add a sentence saying the Context's description of the CI budget guarding the blobless `tickets` checkout no longer holds, because the budget now measures only the code checkout (cc4a23a2405). Alternatively, state explicitly that the ADR Context is deliberately left as a historical record.
evidence: Plan: 'This removes the old sentence "the pack the CI budget guards is blobless". That sentence is wrong today: the budget measures only the code checkout (cc4a23a2405).'
ADR 0106:11-16: 'The CI gate **Verify Authorship Identity** does a *blobless* full-history checkout of that branch ... and fails the build when the checkout pack exceeds a deliberate budget'
ADR 0106:26-29: '...the guarded pack is **blobless** — so folding ... remove **~0** from the guarded pack.'
.github/workflows/verify-identity.yml:31-32: 'the deliberate 102400 KiB (100 MiB) ceiling for the CODE checkout pack, not for the append-only `tickets` event log.'
File impact limits the ADR edit to 'the Follow-up paragraph only'
findings.finding: The plan removes the I1 sentence 'the pack the CI budget guards is blobless' because the budget now measures only the code checkout (cc4a23a2405). But ADR 0106 states the same outdated claim in its Context, and the plan neither lists that spot nor notes it in the rewritten Follow-up. The ADR still says the Verify Authorship Identity gate does a blobless full-history checkout of the `tickets` branch and fails when that pack exceeds the budget. The new I1 text and the new Follow-up both point readers to this ADR as the reclamation contract.
scenarios: A reader follows the new I1 link to ADR 0106 and reads in its Context that the `tickets` pack is CI-budgeted. That contradicts I1's new 'No CI budget applies to it' statement.
findings.suggested_fix: Add this sentence to the end of the replacement Follow-up paragraph: "The Context's description of the CI pack budget no longer holds: since `cc4a23a2405` the `verify-identity.yml` budget measures only the code checkout, which excludes `tickets`, so no CI budget applies to the residual `tickets` pack." The edit stays within the Follow-up hunk, so the 'old-side start is 222 or later' AC still holds.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the `reclaim_collapse\`` AC pattern with a fixed string that excludes `reclaim_collapse_stream` and contains no literal backslash, e.g. `grep -cF -- 'reclaim_collapse`:'`.
evidence: AC definition: "I1 contains X" means ... `grep -cF -- 'X'` (single-quoted, fixed-string)
Module entry listed as: `reclaim_collapse\``
Block line: "- `rebar._commands.reclaim_collapse`: the core-git collapse, with authorship-ledger"
findings.finding: The module-name AC entry `reclaim_collapse\`` cannot pass under the plan's own definition of 'contains' (`grep -cF -- 'X'`). With -F the backslash is a literal character, so the pattern searches for `reclaim_collapse\`` followed by a backtick. The doc text is `rebar._commands.reclaim_collapse`:`, which has no backslash, so the grep prints 0 and the AC fails even when the doc is correct.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'I1 names all 7 modules', entry `reclaim_collapse\``
scenarios: The executor runs the AC literally, gets 0, and either edits the doc wrongly or marks the AC as unmet or flaky.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the fixed string made of reclaim_collapse, a backtick and a colon: `sed -n '/^### I1/,/^### I2/p' docs/concurrency.md | grep -cF -- 'reclaim_collapse`:'`. It prints 1 and does not match `reclaim_collapse_stream`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Rewrite the `reclaim_collapse\`` AC token so the literal fixed string is unambiguous, e.g. 'reclaim_collapse`:' (no backslash), and confirm it matches exactly one line in the proposed I1 block.
evidence: Plan defines: "I1 contains X" means `sed -n '/^### I1/,/^### I2/p' docs/concurrency.md | grep -cF -- 'X'` (single-quoted, fixed-string)
AC item: `reclaim_collapse\``
Proposed block line: "- `rebar._commands.reclaim_collapse`: the core-git collapse, ..." (no backslash)
findings.finding: The module-name AC lists the token `reclaim_collapse\`` with a literal backslash. Under the plan's own definition ('grep -cF -- 'X'', single-quoted, fixed-string), that searches for 'reclaim_collapse\`'. The proposed block contains 'reclaim_collapse`:' with no backslash, so the check prints 0 and the AC falsely fails, or the implementer has to guess what was meant.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'I1 names all 7 modules' bullet, second item `reclaim_collapse\``
scenarios: An implementer or verifier runs `grep -cF -- 'reclaim_collapse\`'` over I1, gets 0, and records a false failure on a correct edit.
A verifier silently drops the backslash, so the proof no longer matches what the AC text states.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the item with a token that needs no escaping in the plan's markdown, e.g. state it as: I1 contains `_commands.reclaim_collapse:` written inside a double-backtick code span, or describe it as "the fixed string reclaim_collapse followed by a backtick". Alternatively use a separate regex check: `grep -cE 'reclaim_collapse`:'`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a pre-edit sweep (`git grep -nE 'specified, in-progress|is specified by \*\*ADR 0106' $B -- docs/`) and state that matches outside the two planned regions are either absent or deliberately left as-is, so the whole-file grep and the hunk-range ACs agree.

"`git diff -U0 $B --stat` lists exactly the 2 files."
Testing: "`make verify` covers the docs-drift, ADR-index and doc-policy tests"
findings.finding: The plan restricts edits to two regions and two files, but it never checks for other references to ADR 0106's old 'specified/in-progress' status that would go stale. Examples: an ADR status/front-matter line above line 222, an ADR index entry, or other concurrency.md sections. Also, if 'specified, in-progress' appears anywhere in the ADR above line 222, the AC `grep -c 'specified, in-progress'` prints 0 over the whole ADR. That AC would then contradict the 'Every ADR hunk's old-side start is 222 or later' AC and the 'exactly the 2 files' stat check.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'Only the planned regions change' and 'The ADR Follow-up is updated'; File impact
scenarios: The ADR header Status reads e.g. 'Accepted — specified, in-progress', so the whole-file grep cannot reach 0 without an out-of-range hunk.
The ADR index lists 0106 with an in-progress status that now contradicts §I1.
